prd.title: Navigateur Agents sur Windows : port natif et qualification indépendante

epics.title: Préparer le host Windows et reprendre les contrats communs

evidence_map.proof: Windows target, CEF/Chromium/cef-rs pins, archive hashes, provenance, protocol version and notices are declared.

evidence_map.entry_point: runtime metadata and Windows native qualification
evidence_map.proof: The signed runtime and same-version development archive were verified on Windows 11 build 26200.0; the manifest declares the Windows 10 1809 floor and bootstrap, sandbox and control-only contracts.

evidence_map.entry_point: explicit fetch and safe extraction CLI
evidence_map.proof: HTTPS provenance, size/SHA-1 when declared/SHA-256 checks, traversal and special-file rejection, bounded extraction and no build.rs or first-use download; fetch security suite passes.
The consumed browser contract commit and protocol version are recorded independently of Linux or another OS qualification.
Absent targets, archive mismatches and unsafe candidates fail closed while an existing runtime is preserved; negative fetch tests pass.
The exported Windows entry point passes sandbox_info, executes subprocess roles before browser initialization, keeps no_sandbox disabled and does not set browser_subprocess_path.
Bootstrap and client roles are separated, x64 PE headers and a real RunWinMain export are required, and unknown client DLLs remain unavailable in contract tests.

evidence_map.entry_point: Windows client build, staging and signature script
evidence_map.proof: The pinned client was built with the same-version CEF development archive, staged with the signed runtime, locally signed for qualification, and executed through the real bootstrap handshake.
Windows runtime discovery is file/manifest based and BrowserRuntime is installed without loading CEF; CEF starts only from a Browser page activation.

evidence_map.entry_point: runtime readiness and staged host verification
evidence_map.proof: Missing or incompatible runtime, bootstrap PE or client export returns unavailable; the supervisor launches the bootstrap executable rather than a DLL and the host requests sandboxing.

evidence_map.entry_point: named-pipe listener and Job Object ownership
evidence_map.proof: The pipe uses owner-scoped SDDL and the bootstrap process is assigned to KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE; no inherited control handle or kill-by-name path is used.
Windows profile tests pass 6/6; production profile creation applies protected SYSTEM, administrators and owner ACLs, and the native receipt reports exactly those entries.
Root locking, ownership, routing, handshake, closure and refused readiness paths are wired; Windows supervisor contract tests pass 4/4 and the native control round trip completed successfully.
Resource release is tied to the owned Job Object and process handles; shutdown has a bounded grace period and no privilege elevation or process-name kill.
Readiness, parent-loss and supervisor failures route to Browser errors while preserving terminal startup and existing profile state.

evidence_map.entry_point: shared BrowserRuntime, authority, ProfileHost and BrowserView
evidence_map.proof: Windows selects target-specific install/supervisor/page adapters while reusing the common controller, dock actions, owners, profiles, descriptors and lifecycle.
The deterministic shared controller path is wired to the Windows ProfileHost and native v3 create/close protocol; no Windows-specific dock rewrite exists.
The target is explicitly development-only, native qualification is not executed, and missing or invalid runtime data leaves public activation unavailable.

evidence_map.entry_point: shared contract metadata and target adapters
evidence_map.proof: The consumed common commit and protocol contract are recorded; the Windows path depends on the shared interfaces, not Linux DONE status or a divergent dock copy.

scope_corrections: Keep EP-001 control-only until EP-002; no native GPU, browser creation or public qualification is claimed.
The review fixed the Windows CEF import-library link emission in build.rs and the common fetch regression caused by an unconditional archive_sha1 lookup.
Runtime packaging remains development-only and must not be treated as Windows sandbox or GPU qualification.

The pinned signed archive and same-version development headers/import library were integrated and qualified through the control-only Windows 11 harness; release signing alignment remains later packaging work.
unapplied_maintenance: Release packaging must align Authenticode signing for chrome_elf.dll, bootstrap and client artifacts.
browser-package.py can make RunWinMain export validation unconditional when release packaging is brought into scope.

epics.title: Implémenter le GPU et obtenir une première preuve Windows

evidence_map.proof: The empty dispatch is replaced by an external_surface pipeline that applies bounds, content mask clip distances and premultiplied blending; native/gpui/checkout carries the applied patch and src-app/src/browser/view.rs:2160 paints the surface on Windows through the shared scene, not through a Windows-only path.

The import checks physical width, height, format, mip levels, array size and sample count, and returns an opaque handle. src-app/src/browser/windows.rs is the only module naming D3D types; the Browser domain sees ExternalSurface plus its generation.

Patches 0010, 0011 and 0012 are declared with the sha256 of the files on disk, verified during this review. The four GPUI revisions in src-app/Cargo.toml and the font-kit feature are untouched by the diff; external_surface_platforms adds windows while the Linux entries and patches 0001 to 0009 stay in place.

presentation.rs is now compiled on Windows, so the 15 FrameConsumer contract tests run on this target and cover pool reservation, import completion, frame intake and release ordering from the harness importer. GPU execution stays attributed to US-008.

The host enables shared textures and implements no on_paint, so there is no CPU refresh fallback. An unsupported format fails in pool_spec with UnsupportedFormat, a stale generation is dropped by the FrameConsumer ledger, and a window without a DirectX surface context refuses page start with an explicit error.

The CEF handle is opened with OpenSharedResource1 inside the callback, validated against the pool description, copied into a host-owned texture and released when the callback returns. The pool textures are shared with DXGI_SHARED_RESOURCE_READ and duplicated only into the client process opened by pid, so the consumer receives bounded rights.

Both sides take key 0 of the same IDXGIKeyedMutex, the producer around CopyResource plus Flush and the consumer around its draw, and a busy key skips the frame instead of blocking. Pool handles are duplicated to the client and closed remotely with DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE; the raw CEF handle is never stored, reused or closed after the callback.

POOL_BUFFERS is 3 and at most two pools coexist, so a replacement holds 6 textures; MAX_PENDING_FRAMES caps in-flight frames at 2. Extra resizes collapse into the single pending_resize slot and the replaced pools are marked retiring, so their generation stops being selected by active_pool.

The callback to publication to consumption path is wired end to end and every exit closes its handles: import_shared_texture closes each handle it consumes, D3dImporter closes the rest on failure, and profile_host_windows closes them when a frame cannot be routed. The FrameConsumer tests cover ownership and release ordering; real fences are observed in US-008.

Device removal, an invalid handle or right, a mismatched description and a retirement older than RETIRE_DEADLINE_MS each emit FrameMessage::Failed with WrongDevice, InvalidHandle, CopyFailed or RetireTimeout. The import runs on a background thread through smol::unblock, and a buffer is only freed when its exact sequence is acknowledged.

Re-read during this review: the log records the DISPLAY1 to DISPLAY2 move, then DISPLAY2 at 150 percent (viewport 1441x881, candidate rect [20,113,12,15]) and at 200 percent (viewport 1266x636, candidate rect [71,113,1,16]), then dpi_restored at 100 percent. The 100 percent candidate rectangles come from the IME corpus of the same run.

evidence_map.entry_point: BrowserView key and mouse handlers -> Command::Input -> host input()
evidence_map.proof: The shared modifier mapping sends Ctrl as MODIFIER_CONTROL, which is the Chromium accelerator modifier on Windows, and the platform key stays MODIFIER_COMMAND. Mouse, wheel, key and IME conversions are wired host side; the browser input handler is scoped to the Browser view, so terminal keystrokes are untouched.

The controller tests cover the candidate rectangle conversion at 100, 125, 150 and 200 percent and the stale geometry rescale. The native corpus archives six cases, ascii, accented, Japanese candidate, astral, cancelled and finished, with 8, 3, 4, 2, 10 and 3 candidate rectangles observed.

evidence_map.entry_point: UiCommand::BindInspector -> devtools::bind and on_native context_menu routing
evidence_map.proof: Menus and the inspector are routed by the shared host client and its DevTools module, and page.rs drops any native event whose document does not match the live document, so a late callback cannot move the focus of another page.

Re-read during this review: focus_lost clears the marked range [15,25], capture_lost is recorded at [720,448], an input addressed to document generation 2 against live generation 1 is refused with StaleGeneration, and the viewport_coordinates step recomputes the centre on the current geometry. The summary counts 6 cancellations and 0 pending expected refusals. The viewport_coordinates condition ran with identical previous and current geometry, so the stale coordinate protection rests on the StaleGeneration refusal.

evidence_map.entry_point: windows-capture.ps1 Get-OsIdentity and the prototype machine event
evidence_map.proof: Microsoft Windows 11 Professionnel, build 26200 UBR 9278, 25H2, x64, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER driver 32.0.16.1656, AMD Radeon 32.0.21045.5002, 33459585024 bytes of RAM, desktop without battery, two displays at 100 percent. The registry ProductName still reads Windows 10 Pro; the build number and the CIM caption carry the identity.

The staging builds the client DLL against the same-version CEF development archive at pin 151.3.24 and stages the signed runtime. Verified during this review: the bootstrap, the client and chrome_elf.dll of the campaign bundle all return a Valid Authenticode status for the single certificate CN=Paneflow EP-001 Native Qualification Fresh, while windows-bootstrap.json records the pre-signature build state. Unsigned (target/ep002-unsigned-probe) and untrusted-issuer (target/ep002-untrusted-probe) trios never complete the bootstrap handshake and record created=false. No MSI or public package is involved.

evidence_map.entry_point: separate Paneflow process -> supervisor -> sandboxed bootstrap
evidence_map.proof: The prototype starts CEF from a separate Paneflow process against the 127.0.0.1:18762 fixture, creates the page (created=true, loaded=true), runs the eight steps and closes the page and its descendants with the sandbox active and exit code 0.

evidence_map.entry_point: shared handle -> owned copy -> GPUI -> input, IME, resize, scale -> close
evidence_map.proof: The fixture really appears in GPUI: 463 frame events, one resize, the monitor change, two DPI transitions with a new pool, the six-case IME corpus and a clean host close in the same run. The M1 campaign confirms the same path over 15 captures.

A, B and C are captured five times each with 10 s warm-up and 60 s measurement, and the comparison refuses captures from different artifacts. 0 unmatched presents over the 15 captures; 1082 input samples in A and 1142 in C, 16715 browser samples in B and 14183 in C. Observed: C minus B p95 613800 ns and p99 807400 ns on browser presentation, C minus A p95 -408700 ns on terminal input, private working set p50 delta 155848704 bytes. The recorded binary_sha256 matches target/release/paneflow.exe built from the reviewed sources; the status stays OBSERVED_NOT_BUDGET_CERTIFIED.

validation.results: Run on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc after the last change. fmt, workspace clippy, host clippy with cef-runtime, cargo deny, the 74 bun tests, py_compile and git diff --check all pass. cargo test --workspace passes 1979 paneflow-app tests plus the host, protocol and harness suites, and fails only the two paneflow-libghostty-sys bundle fixtures that need the Linux and macOS prebuilt archives absent from this Windows worktree; that failure is environmental and outside EP-002.
validation.native: COMPLETE and re-read during this review: target/ep002-input-dpi-r2 records created=true, loaded=true, 463 frames, the 150 and 200 percent transitions with restore, the six-case IME corpus and four cancellation conditions; target/ep002-m1-r0 archives 15 analyzed A, B and C captures with their comparison. The campaign binary_sha256 matches target/release/paneflow.exe, built after the last source edit that preceded the campaign.
validation.native_after_fix: The review fix touches only which RuntimeCheck a dock page selects. The archived binary hash therefore predates the fix while the exercised paths are identical; no native re-run was required.
validation.tracker: US-005, US-006, US-007 and US-008 are DONE; EP-002 is DONE.

remaining_work: Windows public support stays NOT_QUALIFIED: EP-003 and EP-004 carry the package, the release signing, Narrator and the human matrix.
The M1 numbers of target/ep002-m1-r0 are observations on one machine; no NFR budget is declared met before the stories that carry it.
The Windows 10 1809 floor is still unexecuted: the reference machine is Windows 11 build 26200.
The DirectX device recovery re-import required by the external surfaces ADR is not implemented on Windows.
epics.progress_note: EP-002 is certified DONE at the R0 native local tier. The DirectX composition, the D3D11 shared texture ownership, the input, IME and DPI adapters and the first native run are wired from the shared GPUI scene and the shared dock controller, and the native evidence was re-read against the binary that produced it. The review fixed the runtime verification bypass that the qualification digest variable opened in the ordinary dock path. No public support is claimed.

review_findings.criterion: US-008 AC-2 and the PRD runtime integrity constraint
review_findings.defect: RuntimeCheck::configured() honoured PANEFLOW_BROWSER_QUALIFICATION_SHA256 in the ordinary dock path, so any environment carrying that variable replaced the per-file manifest verification of the CEF runtime with an operator supplied digest. Combined with PANEFLOW_CEF_ROOT this loaded an arbitrary runtime tree with no integrity check.
review_findings.correction: RuntimeCheck::dock_session() keeps the manifest check unless an isolated qualification session is configured, that is PANEFLOW_M1_LOG plus an absolute PANEFLOW_M1_STATE_ROOT. BrowserView::start now uses it, the browser-prototype verb keeps the explicit operator path, and a regression test pins the default. The M1 capture harness sets both variables, so the archived campaign behaviour is unchanged.

review_findings.defect: Three blanket allow(dead_code) attributes on ImportedPool, FrameConsumer and its impl block hid every unused item on Windows, which is the exact signal that detects unwired consumer code.
review_findings.correction: The allowances now sit on the six items that are genuinely Linux-only on this target: the ImportedPool layout field and stats, current_size, outstanding, pool_textures and pool_layout.

review_findings.defect: The PageSignal dead-code allowance still claimed the Windows native event mapping was completed by EP-002, while 13 variants stay unconstructed on this target.
review_findings.correction: The reason now names EP-003, which carries the dock controls, the web dialogs and the accessibility bridge.

review_findings.defect: The qualification digest variable was documented as staging configuration without saying that it replaces the runtime verification.
review_findings.correction: The runbook now states what the variable replaces and which session honours it.

review_findings.defect: The Windows present_if_needed passes a constant false for the pending resize flag and does not record resize_sent or resize_ready, so a burst of geometry changes relies entirely on the host pending_resize slot and the M1 resize latency instrumentation stays Linux only.
review_findings.correction: Left as is: no EP-002 criterion covers the resize latency signal, coalescing is proven host side, and the change would invalidate the archived native evidence.

review_findings.defect: The paneflow watch clap help text carries an (EP-002) tracker marker in user-visible copy. It predates this epic.

No CI job runs the bun suites under scripts/browser-qualification, so windows-analysis.test.mjs and windows-m1-compare.test.mjs are local gates only, like the pre-existing fetch and qualification suites.

scope_corrections: The Windows target stays availability = development: EP-002 certifies the R0 native path, not a public Browser release.
The M1 figures are single-machine observations on Windows 11 build 26200; no NFR budget is declared met.

The GPU device recovery contract of docs/browser/gpui-external-surfaces.md is not implemented on Windows: LivePage keeps the ExternalSurfaceContext captured at start and does not compare the device identity after a renderer recreation. No EP-002 criterion covers it; it belongs with the later Windows resilience work.
unapplied_maintenance: Compare the ExternalSurfaceContext identity after a DirectX device recovery and re-import the pool, as the external surfaces ADR requires.
Give the Windows present_if_needed the same pending-resize tracking and resize_sent/resize_ready instrumentation as the Linux path.
Add the browser-qualification bun suites to a CI job so they stop being local-only gates.

epics.title: Compléter les intégrations OS et préparer le package Windows
notes: The manifest now carries the measured Windows codec table, so its digest changed from 32567aed09e90c13100ee30fecd0b6ad05f20eee2133cf04ba5f7fce6e56bdc0 to 2d9e7de8602bf309ba4c59f6458ba374422d65ce9e8f2cda97605d2f83e7572a. Every staged prefix has to be re-staged; the EP-001 and EP-002 native observations depend on the binaries, not on the manifest text, and are unaffected.
Drag-and-drop file upload and the renderer clipboard round trip stay Linux-only: US-010 lists neither, and the Windows copy path uses the Chromium clipboard directly.
Agent console and network diagnostics are still not emitted by the Windows host; they belong to US-016.
The bounded host DLL search path has a contract test and the bundle import inventory as proof; its native launch observation belongs to US-013.

evidence_map.entry_point: CEF Renderer::accessibility_handler -> accessibility::Accessibility -> control pipe -> LivePage::on_native -> PageSignal::Accessibility -> AccessibilityTree -> GPUI A11ySubtreeBuilder
evidence_map.proof: The Windows client enables the accessibility state on creation and mounts the shared CEF accessibility handler, so tree and location updates carry their document identity to the shared bridge that GPUI publishes to the platform. browser::page::windows::tests::accessibility_updates_reach_the_shared_tree_for_the_live_document drives one real host event end to end.

evidence_map.entry_point: Browser actions -> find/zoom/cycle_focus and the shared toolbar render on Windows
evidence_map.proof: Search, zoom, reset, F6 focus cycling, visible focus and the U1 color roles are the shared dock controls; the Windows host now emits find_result and the shared view consumes it. Accessibility state is bound to the document generation through accessibility_document in view.rs:1240.

The bridge controller test feeds real accessibility_tree and accessibility_unavailable host events through native_signals and asserts the emitted PageSignal plus the resulting AccessKit snapshot. The Narrator pass is prepared and explicitly left to US-013.

evidence_map.entry_point: accessibility_unavailable or a stale/oversized update -> AccessibilityTree::apply
evidence_map.proof: A stale node, an unavailable subframe or a missing tree clears the nodes and marks the tree unavailable instead of fabricating content; a replaced document drops updates outright (browser::page::windows::tests::accessibility_updates_for_a_replaced_document_are_dropped).

evidence_map.entry_point: BrowserClient dialog/download/permission/jsdialog handlers -> control pipe -> BrowserView::handle_transfer -> GPUI prompt_for_paths / prompt_for_new_path
evidence_map.proof: File pickers, download destinations, camera/microphone and clipboard-read requests and external protocols all reach the shared controllers, which use the GPUI native Windows dialogs and dirs::download_dir. The host never accepts an arbitrary path; external protocols are limited to mailto/tel/sms/magnet and open only after a human answer.

evidence_map.entry_point: CEF permission callback -> latest_document -> web_dialog -> InputEvent::WebResponse -> permissions::handle
evidence_map.proof: P1 stays the only policy: the origin is re-parsed and restricted to https or loopback http, the mask is limited to geolocation and clipboard (or audio/video capture), and the decision is re-checked against the live document generation when the asynchronous OS answer returns. A strict certificate policy is enforced on the request context before the page loads (windows.rs enforce_certificate_policy).

Tests inject grant, refusal, closure and concurrent navigation through the permission and file controllers: web_dialog/web_dialog_closed, file_picker, download_destination and download_progress, plus a replaced document that drops every one of them. Request 0 and an oversized suggested name are refused.

An OS refusal, an absent capability, a closed dialog or a late callback grants nothing: navigation, renderer crash and close all clear the pending permissions, dialogs, transfers and external protocols, and no download is executed automatically. Certificate errors cancel the callback and surface a load failure.

evidence_map.entry_point: python scripts/browser-package.py --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc stage; pwsh scripts/browser-msi.ps1
evidence_map.proof: The staged prefix carries the bootstrap, the client DLL, libcef, the resources and every locale, and the generated BrowserRuntime component group installs them under %ProgramFiles%\PaneFlow\lib\paneflow, which a standard user cannot modify. Verified on the real staged payload: 246 components.

The chain signs exactly the two components PaneFlow produces through the existing runbook, re-verifies against the signed bytes, and refuses to build without the maintainer signing variables. The runtime_imports check proves no bundled PE depends on a module outside the bundle, the Windows system set or the Microsoft C runtime, and supervisor_windows::host_search_path removes the user PATH from the child search order.

Eleven fixture tests cover component coverage, receipt exclusion, unique identifiers and GUIDs, the WiX fragment shape, a foreign import, a wrong-architecture image, a payload edited after planning, a missing plan, plan stability and the codec measurement. Building the real signed MSI and installing it belong to US-013.

main.wxs keeps its published terminal-only output behind the preprocessor guard, the shim, ai-hook and MCP helpers are untouched, and the signing secrets are read from the maintainer environment listed in docs/release/windows-signing.md, never from the repository.

A missing resource, a non-x86_64 image, a path escaping the bundle or an absent signing configuration blocks the distributable build; browser-msi.ps1 prints distributable false and stops. Nothing in the chain downloads the runtime, in build.rs or on first use.

The Windows updater refuses to replace the MSI while a browser host holds the runtime files, and the relay waits for the PaneFlow process to exit while the Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE takes the descendants with it. A runtime stamped by another manifest is reported unusable rather than mixed (install_windows::classify).

evidence_map.entry_point: browser::update::site -> install::required_bytes and install::detect; ProfileStore marker
evidence_map.proof: The plan reads the payload size and the runtime state from the shared manifest and its digest stamp; the profile marker records the engine that wrote it, refuses a profile written by a newer engine and migrates an older one through a temporary file and a rename, so no downgrade rewrites data.

Fixtures cover a retained runtime file, an interrupted installation reported as resumable, an installation drive without room, an unreadable drive that invents no verdict, and a terminal-only installation. The real native update belongs to US-013.

The codec table is measured on the pinned runtime through the FFmpeg decoder long names, so the SBOM reports restricted_codecs [aac, h264, hevc] and redistribution review_required. Licenses, credits and notices are checked in the same verdict, and the pin maintenance runbook states explicitly that cargo deny never covers this runtime.

An invalid stamp or a partial set keeps the previous availability absent with a repair reason instead of opening a page, and the profile store refuses a profile written by an incompatible engine. Signature verification of the MSI itself stays in update::windows::msi::windows_verify_trust.

commands: cargo clippy -p paneflow-browser-host --features cef-runtime --all-targets --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings
python scripts/browser-package.py --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc verify --format msi --prefix target/browser-stage
validation.results: Run on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc after the last change. fmt, workspace clippy and the 12 bundle-plan tests pass. The Windows CEF host is the code US-009 and US-010 add, and the default workspace build compiles none of it: it sits behind feature cef-runtime, which CI only builds for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu. It was therefore clippied and tested explicitly for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc against the local CEF development root; 7 host tests and 2 qualification tests pass with -D warnings clean. paneflow-app passes 1994 of 1995 tests, including the 96 browser tests and the 7 new page::windows, install and update fixtures; the single failure is files_sidebar::filter::fifty_thousand_entries_filter_under_the_frame_budget at 67.45ms against a 64ms budget under parallel load, and it passes in isolation. cargo test --workspace additionally fails paneflow-textdiff::a_side_over_twenty_thousand_chunks_is_too_big, which also passes in isolation, and the two paneflow-libghostty-sys bundle fixtures that need the Linux and macOS prebuilt archives absent from this Windows worktree. All three are environmental and outside EP-003. browser-package.py verify --format msi returns PASS on the real 246-component staged payload, and browser-msi.ps1 runs the whole chain to the signing gate and reports distributable false with the six missing Azure variables.
validation.native: NONE. EP-003 claims no native Windows observation: no MSI was built, installed or signed, no Narrator pass was run and no native update cycle was executed. WiX v3 is not installed on this machine and the signing secrets are not present, so cargo wix itself was not executed; the corrected --include arguments are proven against the cargo-wix 0.3.9 source and the identical invocation the release workflow already uses. Those observations belong to US-013.
validation.tracker: US-009, US-010, US-011 and US-012 are DONE; EP-003 is DONE.

review_findings.defect: The MSI chain could never build. cargo wix was invoked with neither WiX source: cargo-wix 0.3.9 does not read the wxs key of [package.metadata.wix] and only auto-discovers src-app/wix/*.wxs, which does not exist in this repository, so the call stops on Error[2] There are no WXS files. Even past that, the generated browser-components.wxs was never handed to candle, so the ComponentGroupRef Id='BrowserRuntime' that main.wxs adds behind <?ifdef BrowserStage ?> had no referent and light would fail on an unresolved symbol. The whole generated component group was unreachable from the build. The release workflow already documents this cargo-wix behaviour at .github/workflows/release.yml:1374 and passes --include for the terminal-only MSI.
review_findings.correction: browser-msi.ps1 now passes --include for packaging/wix/main.wxs and for the staged browser-components.wxs, and its comment-based help states why. Verified against the cargo-wix 0.3.9 create.rs wxs_sources implementation, which extends the auto-discovered set with every --include path.

review_findings.defect: The SBOM that ships inside the MSI was stamped format 'stage', because stage writes it before the plan and the chain never restamped it. Running the documented sbom --format msi afterwards rewrote a packaged file and silently invalidated every plan digest; verify --format msi then reported a real msi_plan FAIL on the local staged payload.
review_findings.correction: browser-msi.ps1 restamps share/doc/paneflow/browser-sbom.json for the msi format before regenerating the plan, so the plan digest covers the bytes the MSI ships. verify --format msi now returns PASS on the real 246-component payload.

review_findings.defect: wix_identifier truncated the stem to 70 characters and then appended an underscore and eight hexadecimal digits, so it could emit a 79-character identifier while the MSI Component, File and Directory Identifier columns hold 72. The current payload peaks at 70, so the trap was latent, and the existing test asserted <= 79, codifying it.
review_findings.correction: The stem is capped at WIX_IDENTIFIER_LIMIT - 9 so every generated identifier fits 72 characters, the existing test asserts the real ceiling, and a new test drives a 120-character path plus every identifier of a generated fragment through it.

review_findings.defect: The installed-layout block listed browser/Resources/... and browser/Resources/locales/..., which do not exist on Windows: the pinned CEF Windows archive keeps icudtl.dat, the pak files and locales inside Release/, and the staged tree has no Resources directory at all.
review_findings.correction: The block now matches the staged tree, and the packaging section states why both WiX sources are named explicitly and that the SBOM is restamped.

review_findings.defect: The permission module is now compiled into the Windows host, but its test module was narrowed to #[cfg(all(test, target_os = "linux"))], so the P1 policy fixtures do not run on Windows.
review_findings.correction: Left as is, after verifying it: un-gating the module fails to compile with six errors because the fixtures build the Linux-only HOST, Host and Page items of linux.rs, which windows.rs does not have. Running them on Windows needs a Windows page fixture, a scope expansion. The Windows path is covered instead by the shared browser::page::windows tests that drive grant, refusal, closure and a replaced document through the app-side controller.

review_findings.defect: emit no longer returns io::Result on Windows, so on_before_context_menu stopped cancelling a pending menu when the control pipe write fails. A dead pipe now leaves the menu registered with a live CEF callback until the next navigation or close.
review_findings.correction: Left as is: the control loop quits the message loop on the next failed protocol reply, clear_web_state and editing::cancel run on navigation, renderer crash and close, and no EP-003 criterion covers a broken control pipe. Worth revisiting with the host resilience work.

review_findings.defect: web_interactions, permissions and external_protocols each allocate request ids from their own counter, and a single InputEvent::WebResponse is dispatched to all three. Two modules can therefore hold the same id, and the automatic refusal the view sends for a second dialog can resolve the first module's pending request. The outcome is fail-closed, never a grant. The same dispatch predates this epic in linux/presentation.rs:507 and belongs to the shared socle.
review_findings.correction: Not changed by this review: the fix belongs to the Linux-owned shared controllers, outside the EP-003 boundary.

review_findings.defect: No CI job compiles paneflow-browser-host with feature cef-runtime for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc; only aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu is covered. Every line the Windows host adds is therefore unlinted and untested by CI, and was only proven here by an explicit local run against the CEF development root.

epics.progress_note: EP-003 is certified DONE at the implementation tier. The accessibility bridge, the permission, dialog and file paths, the MSI bundle plan and the update plan are reachable from their real entry points: the CEF client mounts the shared handlers, native_signals maps every scoped event to the shared PageSignal the dock already consumes, kickoff_self_update_install gates the Windows install on browser::update::plan, and browser-package.py stage generates the WiX component group the MSI feature references. The review fixed the packaging chain, which could not build the MSI at all, and the SBOM restamp that invalidated the plan. No native Windows observation is claimed.

epics.title: Qualifier et préparer les livraisons Windows
epics.scope_note: The qualification contract, its verifier, the CI wiring, the code-level availability ceiling, the Windows 10 floor enforcement, the Windows agent diagnostics and navigation lifecycle, the adapter identity trace and its LUID pin, and the report and usage documents are implemented and wired. Native work on record: the agent navigation lifecycle with stale refusal and human takeover, the adapter pin on both adapters including the split assignment, and two M1 campaigns under the corrected harness whose thirty captures all prove foreground ownership. The owner waived the Windows 10 1809 run on 2026-09-11. NFR-03 is within budget at both refresh rates and NFR-02 at 60 Hz; NFR-02 at 120 Hz sits 0.106 ms over budget on a delta the method cannot resolve. Both release verdicts stay NOT_QUALIFIED and the epic remains IN_PROGRESS.

evidence_map.proof: The gpu-displays row records two adapters that each drove the presentation path natively on Windows 11 build 26200: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER 0x10de:0x2705 with 167 frame events and a first frame after 3360 ms (target/ep004-gpu-nvidia2), and AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics 0x1002:0x164e with 167 frame events and a first frame after 2726 ms (target/ep004-gpu-amd-run). The adapter identity comes from the paneflow-browser-adapter line the host now emits at D3D11 device creation. The split adapter assignment that used to fail with 0x80070057 now presents: the application passes its D3D11 adapter LUID to the host, which opens that adapter with EnumAdapterByLuid and forwards the LUID to Chromium as --use-adapter-luid. target/ep004-gpu-split-pin COMPLETED with 277 frame events and a first frame after 2787 ms, target/ep004-gpu-split-forced COMPLETED with 276 frame events under opposite explicit preferences per image, and target/ep004-gpu-default-pin COMPLETED with 272 frame events with no preference at all. The row stays NOT_EXECUTED: no display pair with different scale factors and no switchable-graphics laptop has been covered.

The distribution row names an Authenticode-signed MSI, a standard-user installation, a protected-directory start, the loaded-DLL check and the hostile-DLL refusal, and declares that no release signing certificate exists on this machine. native_release_qualified stays false.

The owner waived the native Windows 10 1809 run on 2026-09-11 in favor of code and tests. The minimum-product row carries the decider, the date, the reason, four code-evidence entries and two residual risks; the verifier refuses a waiver missing any of those and refuses one presenting native evidence it does not have. The floor itself is enforced at src-app/src/browser/install_windows.rs:81 and applied by detect before the runtime is classified.

The current-reference row still needs a frozen reference build, a human Narrator pass and an installed-package journey. None of the three is reachable from this machine without a human driving a rendered session.
A row that claims execution without an evidence path and a machine identity is rejected, and so is a row that claims partial coverage without a machine identity. Eight tests pass.

Both M1 A/B/C campaigns were re-run under the corrected harness on an untouched machine: target/ep004-m1-120hz-v2 at the 120 Hz mode and target/ep004-m1-60hz-v2 at the 59.94 Hz mode, five repetitions per configuration at a 1920x1080 physical viewport. All thirty captures report window_foreground ratio 1, zero unmatched presents and at most one dropped present. They carry NFR-02 and NFR-03. The performance row stays NOT_EXECUTED: NFR-02 at 120 Hz sits 0.106 ms over its p95 budget on a delta the method cannot resolve, GPU memory is not sampled, interop allocations are not separated from internal Chromium VRAM, and six NFR rows have no campaign.

NFR-02 and NFR-03 are MEASURED again from captures that can prove foreground ownership. NFR-03 is WITHIN_BUDGET at both rates: C over B p95 0.100 ms at 60 Hz and -0.122 ms at 120 Hz against a 2 ms budget. NFR-02 is WITHIN_BUDGET at 60 Hz at 0.006 ms p95 and 0.106 ms over the 1 ms budget at 120 Hz, where the p99 delta is negative and the two configurations measure 42.90 and 44.00 ms, so the excess is below what medians of per-repetition percentiles resolve. The eight remaining NFR rows stay NOT_MEASURED.

Recovery after a host restart has no native receipt. Recovery after a human takeover is now proven: target/ep004-agent-r11 cancels the pending agent operation with Err(Unavailable) when a human navigation supersedes it.
A budget declared MEASURED without an evidence path is rejected.
The verdict rule keeps human_release NOT_QUALIFIED while any matrix row is neither WORKS_MEASURED nor WAIVED_BY_OWNER, any security case is unproven, or any budget is unmeasured.

evidence_map.entry_point: the versioned Windows release report and its contract
evidence_map.proof: The report carries the S1-W matrix and release verdict section, the Windows 10 1809 waiver, the adapter results of the Which GPU drove the presentation section, and a Qualification still required list that matches the contract rows. No Linux or macOS result is offered as Windows evidence.

The Windows availability the application exposes is clamped by the contract verdicts, so a promoted manifest alone never exposes a qualified capability. Covered by a_promoted_manifest_stays_development_until_the_windows_verdict_changes.

The usage guide documents the installation layout, the page journey, the default keys, the errors, the local data location, the permission dialogs, DevTools, agent access and what is not qualified yet. The verifier refuses a contract whose documents do not resolve to written files.

human_release and agent_release are both NOT_QUALIFIED, native_release_evidence_required is true, foreign_platform_evidence_accepted is false, and the manifest availability for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc stays development under the ceiling the verifier enforces.

evidence_map.entry_point: CEF client handlers -> agent_console, agent_network and agent_navigation_committed -> the control thread Controller
evidence_map.proof: The Windows client emits agent console messages and network events and terminalizes an agent navigation at the main-document commit rather than at acknowledgement, and the whole lifecycle is now observed natively against the current binary: target/ep004-agent-r11/prototype.jsonl ends on status COMPLETED with op-4 leaving AwaitCommit on Ok(Completed), op-5 refused with Err(StaleGeneration) and op-6 cancelled by the human takeover with Err(Unavailable).

The agent row stays NOT_EXECUTED. The navigation lifecycle, stale generations and human takeover now carry a native receipt, but a host restart, the C3 quotas at their limit and limit plus one, two workspaces, two clients and SEC-12 do not. Those need a session where a human has granted agent access, which src-app/src/browser/browser_dock.rs reaches only from the Browser menu: no IPC or qualification path grants it.
Identities, origin, generation and timestamps travel with every agent event on the Windows path as on the others.
Access starts disabled per workspace, read authorizes no mutation, and any revocation is immediate.
An invalid scope, a lost lease or an unproven agent matrix keeps agent_release NOT_QUALIFIED, and the manifest may not declare agent_qualified under that verdict.

scope_corrections: The Windows client emitted no agent console or network diagnostics and never terminalized an agent navigation; both are now implemented, and the Windows control thread shares its Controller with the CEF UI thread so the main-document commit can produce a new document generation.
The Windows availability ceiling is now enforced in code at install_windows::declared_availability, the function BrowserAuthority::detect calls, instead of resting on documentation alone.

The declared Windows 10 floor was a dead declaration: the manifest named minimum_windows 10.0.17763 and nothing read it. install_windows::floor_verdict now refuses a host below the declared build and refuses an unreadable build number, and detect applies that verdict before the runtime is classified.

The host created its D3D11 device with no explicit adapter and never recorded which GPU Windows handed it, so every GPU claim was unfalsifiable. The host now emits one paneflow-browser-adapter line at device creation carrying the description, the vendor and device identifiers, the dedicated video memory and the LUID.

Two claims first written into this contract were wrong and were corrected against the data: the retained EP-002 campaign does not need a viewport assertion because the analyzer already refuses any capture that is not 1920x1080 physical, and browser_callback_to_present is not empty, it carries 16715 samples in configuration B and 14183 in configuration C, only the no-Browser witness having none by construction.

The owner waived the native Windows 10 1809 run on 2026-09-11. The waiver is a first-class contract status, WAIVED_BY_OWNER, with mandatory decider, date, reason, code evidence and residual risk, not a silently relaxed row.
Two M1 A/B/C campaigns were run natively after the owner authorized the display-mode changes they require, which the first handoff had listed as a blocker.

The native GPU matrix was partially closed by forcing each adapter per executable image, which exposed a split-adapter presentation failure that is now fixed by pinning the browser host and the CEF GPU process to the application adapter, and re-proven on the split, the adversarial split and the unforced pairing.

The agent navigation never terminalized because the Windows LivePage in src-app/src/browser/page.rs carried no branch for agent_navigation_committed, agent_navigation_failed or agent_navigation_cancelled: native_signals dropped the whole family through its unscoped_signals fallback, silently. The Linux adapter had always handled them. The Windows branches are now present and unit-covered, and a cancellation is scoped to the page rather than to the exact live document, because a human takeover always supersedes the generation the pending operation was issued against.

Every navigation also fired a D3D11 RetireTimeout one second later, because the FrameAck routing in crates/paneflow-browser-host/src/windows.rs demanded page.document == document: each frame release belonging to the superseded generation was discarded, so the retiring pool never drained. Routing now accepts an acknowledgement from the same owner at or below the live generation, and the presenter still validates the pool document and sequence before freeing a slot.

The prototype agent step itself had two sequencing faults: its deliberately stale navigation never armed expected_refusals, so the expected StaleGeneration refusal failed the run, and its human takeover was built from the document captured before the second agent navigation was acknowledged, which made the takeover itself stale. The step now arms the refusal and waits for the acknowledged generation before taking the page back.

The terminal latency regression reported earlier in this epic does not exist. Re-measuring it found that the M1 per-repetition p95 is bimodal in every campaign, including the binary that was supposed to be clean, and that the discriminator is whether the benchmark window held the foreground: a background window is throttled by Windows, so the input waits for the next frame of a slowed redraw loop. A controlled experiment stealing the foreground mid-capture reproduces the drop exactly (445, 445, 427, 74, 74, 74, ... presents per slice, target/probe-steal-01). The defect was in the measurement harness, which accepted such captures silently, and it is now refused at three levels.
blockers: NFR-02 at 120 Hz cannot be closed on the current method: the p95 overhead exceeds its budget by 0.106 ms while the p99 overhead is negative, which describes no single distribution. Settling it needs paired per-repetition deltas or more repetitions, not a correction designed on this figure.

No release signing certificate is available here, so the signed MSI, the standard-user installation, the protected-directory start and the loaded-DLL checks of the distribution row cannot be executed.
The C0 and U1/U2 reference journey, the native SEC-02, SEC-04 and SEC-05 cases and the Narrator pass need a human driving a rendered session on frozen reference builds.

The rest of the agent row needs a human to grant agent access first: access starts disabled per workspace by design and is reachable only from the Browser menu, with no IPC or qualification path. Until an operator grants it in a live session, the C3 quotas, two workspaces, two clients, the host restart and SEC-12 cannot be exercised natively.
remaining_work: Change the M1 comparison to pair repetitions before taking a delta, or raise the repetition count, then re-read NFR-02 at 120 Hz.

Complete the campaigns for NFR-01, NFR-04, NFR-05, NFR-06, NFR-08, NFR-11 and NFR-13, add GPU memory sampling, separate interop allocations from internal Chromium VRAM, and compute the C over B integration delta NFR-07 needs.

Run a native agent session in which an operator has granted agent access, covering the C3 quotas at their limit and limit plus one, two workspaces, two clients, a host restart and SEC-12, then promote the agent row from its receipt.
Run the journey, accessibility and update campaigns on a frozen Windows 11 reference with a human Narrator pass, and cover a display pair with different scale factors.
Sign a real MSI through the release chain, install it as a standard user on a clean machine and verify the loaded modules and the hostile-DLL refusal.
Run the adapter pin on a switchable-graphics laptop, which is the only pairing the desktop cannot represent.

Only after every row is measured or waived, change human_release and then agent_release in the contract and raise the manifest availability; the verifier and install_windows::declared_availability enforce that order.
